chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadani, from Abu Saeed al-Shami, who said: Salih ibn Uqba informed me, saying: I heard Al-Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him) say:
It is recommended to involve the child in hard work during his young age so that he becomes forbearing in his old age.
Then he said: It is not befitting except if it happens like this.

key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الصَّالِحَ: The pious servant (a title for Imam Musa al-Kazim, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended approach to raising children to develop patience and character according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia pedagogical principle of 'tarbiyah bi-l-tajribah' (education through experience), where enduring hardship in youth builds resilience (hilm) for adulthood. The Imam’s concluding affirmation underscores that this deliberate cultivation of endurance is not merely optional but the normative standard for raising virtuous individuals. It reflects the broader Shia emphasis on practical character formation over mere theoretical knowledge.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Ali Al Hamdany, from Abu Saeed Al Shamy, from Salih Bin Uqba who said, 
‘I heard Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘It is recommended to (involve) the child in hard-work during his young age in order for him to become forbearing in his old age’.
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not befitting except if it happens like this’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar from his father from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hamadaniy from abu Sa‘d al-Shamiy who has said that Salih ibn ‘Uqbah narrated to me saying the following: “I heard the virtuous servant of Allah saying, ‘
It is preferable to involve a child in difficult tasks when he is small, so he can be forbearing when he grows up.’
He (the Imam) then said, ‘It is not proper to be other than as such.’”
